_comment: Unique buildings carry `clan` (only that clan builds them) and `effects`, added per level to the village's bonuses. Village layout: `fields` are the resource plots around the village (one building type each, upgraded individually); a village founded by settlers takes its fields from the land within `outpostRange` instead (one of each kind, the rest shared out by what the outposts' `yields` say that land gives; starting villages and refugee camps keep the balanced `fields`); the center has `centerSlots` building slots, the first holding the Elder's Hall. Each Hall level above 1 unlocks `slotsPerHallLevel` more slots, every `hallLevelsPerQueueSlot` levels add a build-queue place, and each level speeds construction by `hallBuildSpeedup`. Outposts are claimed on resource hexes within `outpostRange` of the village; a village may hold `baseOutposts` plus one per `hallLevelsPerOutpost` Hall levels. An outpost's yield per hour depends on its hex's terrain (`yields`), multiplied by `yieldGrowth` per level above 1. Each terrain's outpost has its own name and look (`kinds`: a Farmstead on plains, a Sawmill in forests, a Quarry in hills, a Woodland camp on wooded hills, a Mine in mountains, a Fishing boat on a lake); the rules are the same. A building marked `multiple` may stand in more than one slot (its effects add up; storehouses add their capacity); one with `requires` needs those buildings at those levels first; one with `site` only where the land allows it: `water` for a village beside a lake or on a river (one of its six edges a river's), `hills` for a village on hills. Demolishing a building gives the village back `demolishRefund` of everything it cost; cancelling a build in the queue gives back `cancelRefund.base` of what it cost, plus `cancelRefund.perHallLevel` per Elder's Hall level above 1 (at most all), and later levels of the same plot go with it; abandoning a whole village sends `abandonRefund` of everything that stood there to the Holy City vault. The Academy brings in research per hour (`research`), the player's own, which techs cost. The Market trades at `market.baseRate`, plus `ratePerLevel` per level above 1 (what one resource fetches of another), and buys a spare piece of the hero's gear for `gearValue`. Its bounty board (`bounties`): a village with a Market posts an offer of resources for others; what it offers is paid at once, with `feeShare` of it on top as a fee, and when another player takes it (paying what is asked, at once) the poster gets what was asked less `feeShare`. A Market keeps one open bounty, plus one every `levelsPerBounty` levels above 1, each offering and asking at most `amountPerLevel` x its level in all. A bounty can be called off at any time: what it offers comes back, the fee does not. (A solo world has no bounty board.) A building with `embers` takes that many of the group's Svarog's Embers for every level (given back in full when the build is cancelled). The Shrine also has `deities`: its village picks one god, whose `effects` times the Shrine's level add to the owner's bonuses in all their villages; turning to another god takes `switchEmbers` Embers.

elder_hall.name: Elder's Hall
elder_hall.description: The heart of the village. Each level opens two more building slots, builds faster and allows another outpost; most levels add a place in the build queue.

woodcutter.name: Woodcutter
woodcutter.description: Cuts wood in the forest around the village.

quarry.name: Quarry
quarry.description: Breaks stone from the hills around the village.

farm.name: Farm
farm.description: Grows grain, which feeds the village and its troops.

iron_mine.name: Iron Mine
iron_mine.description: Digs iron for weapons, armour and walls.

storehouse.name: Storehouse
storehouse.description: How much of each resource the village can keep; what comes in above it is lost. A village may build more than one.

barracks.name: Barracks
barracks.description: Trains infantry. Each level trains them faster, and higher levels open stronger troops.

stables.name: Stables
stables.description: Breeds horses and trains riders. Each level trains them faster, and higher levels open stronger riders.

shooting_range.name: Shooting Range
shooting_range.description: Trains archers, skirmishers and throwers. Each level trains them faster, and higher levels open stronger shooters.

heroes_hall.name: Hero's Hall
heroes_hall.description: Recruits generals, who lead armies and command garrisons. Each level lets the hero recover from wounds faster here, and each level above the first allows another general.

scout_lodge.name: Scout Lodge
scout_lodge.description: Trains scouts, who ride out to see a horde before it arrives.

caravan_yard.name: Caravan Yard
caravan_yard.description: Keeps caravans to carry resources to allies and to the Holy City vault; each level adds more.

settlers_lodge.name: Settlers' Lodge
settlers_lodge.description: Trains settlers, who walk out to found new villages.

shrine.name: Shrine
shrine.description: A shrine to one of the old gods, raised with a Svarog's Ember. Choose its god: the blessing reaches all your villages and grows with every level (turning to another god takes an Ember). Each level takes another Ember and mostly grain, the offering.

perun.name: Perun
perun.description: The thunderer, god of war: your troops strike harder.

svetovid.name: Svetovid
svetovid.description: The four-faced watcher: your villages hold better.

veles.name: Veles
veles.description: Lord of herds: more grain, and troops eat less.

mokosh.name: Mokosh
mokosh.description: The mother who spins fate: fuller stores, and raiders carry off less.

svarog.name: Svarog
svarog.description: The heavenly smith: you build and train faster.

dazhbog.name: Dazhbog
dazhbog.description: The giving sun: every resource flows a little richer.

stribog.name: Stribog
stribog.description: Grandfather of the winds: caravans and scouts travel faster, and more scouts come home.

academy.name: Academy
academy.description: Studies the techs of the research tree and brings in the research every tech costs; what you learn helps all your villages.

outpost.name: Outpost
outpost.description: A camp on a nearby hex that gathers what the land gives: wood in forests, stone and iron in hills and mountains, grain on plains and lakes.

plains.name: Farmstead
plains.description: Fields and a barn on the open plain: grain.

forest.name: Sawmill
forest.description: A saw pit and log piles in the woods: wood.

hills.name: Quarry
hills.description: Stone cut from the hillside, and the iron in it.

wooded_hills.name: Woodland camp
wooded_hills.description: Loggers and stonecutters on the wooded hills: a little of everything.

mountain.name: Mine
mountain.description: A shaft into the mountain: stone and iron.

lake.name: Fishing boat
lake.description: Nets cast from a boat on the lake: fish for the granary.

granary_temple.name: Granary-Temple
granary_temple.description: The stag-folk's own: a temple granary that brings in grain and feeds the troops for less.

stone_redoubt.name: Stone Redoubt
stone_redoubt.description: The bear-folk's own: a stone keep that makes the garrison harder to break.

longhouse_hall.name: Longhouse Hall
longhouse_hall.description: The wolf-folk's own: a longhouse where warriors eat less and train faster.

wall.name: Walls
wall.description: The walls round the village: hordes must break or climb them before they reach the garrison. Higher levels change wood for stone.

archer_tower.name: Archer Tower
archer_tower.description: A tower on the walls: its archers make the garrison strike harder while the walls stand.

gate_tower.name: Gate Tower
gate_tower.description: Strengthens the gate, so the walls take longer to batter down.

ballista.name: Ballista Platform
ballista.description: A great crossbow on the walls that smashes the horde's siege engines.

murder_holes.name: Murder Holes
murder_holes.description: Openings over the gate to rain stones on the attackers: the garrison defends better while the walls stand.

ditch.name: Moat
ditch.description: A moat before the walls: it keeps off battering and climbers and slows the building of siege engines; at higher levels it holds water.

watchtower.name: Watchtower
watchtower.description: Sees hordes coming from farther away, so the warning comes sooner.

forester.name: Forester
forester.description: Tends the woods so they grow back thick: 5% more wood per level, from fields and outposts alike. Needs a Woodcutter of level 3.

stonemason.name: Stonemason
stonemason.description: Dresses the stone as it comes in: 5% more stone per level. Needs a Quarry of level 3.

mill.name: Mill
mill.description: Grinds the grain so less goes to waste: 5% more grain per level. Needs a Farm of level 3.

smelter.name: Smelter
smelter.description: Smelts the ore hotter: 5% more iron per level. Needs an Iron Mine of level 3.

hospital.name: Hospital
hospital.description: Tends the wounded: when the garrison holds its own village, 10% per level of its fallen get up again.

masons_guild.name: Masons' Guild
masons_guild.description: Master builders who teach the village's hands the craft: every building goes up 4% faster per level.

workers_huts.name: Workers' Huts
workers_huts.description: Homes for the hands who work the fields, woods, quarries and mines: 4% more of every resource per level.

grain_silo.name: Grain Silo
grain_silo.description: A tall store for grain alone: the village keeps more grain, for its people, its garrison and the armies it feeds. A village may build more than one.

fisherman_hut.name: Fisherman's Hut
fisherman_hut.description: Nets and weirs on the water beside the village bring in fish: grain every hour, more each level. Only for a village beside a lake or on a river.

water_wheel.name: Water Wheel
water_wheel.description: The river turns the wheel and the wheel turns the work: 3% more of every resource and 3% faster building per level. Only for a village beside a lake or on a river.

windmill.name: Windmill
windmill.description: Sails on the hilltop grind the grain finer: 6% more grain per level. Only for a village on hills.

ranch.name: Ranch
ranch.description: Herds graze the open plains: grain every hour, more each level, and the village's riders come from better horses, 2% stronger per level (10% at the top). Only for a village on the plains.

mountain_lodge.name: Mountain Lodge
mountain_lodge.description: Miners, quarrymen and woodcutters who know the mountain's slopes: 5% more wood, stone and iron per level. Only for a village next to a mountain.

blacksmith.name: Blacksmith
blacksmith.description: Forges better arms, armor and harness for one kind of unit at a time: sharper attack, stouter defense, tougher troops, a faster march. What you forge serves all your villages. Each level forges 6% faster and higher levels forge the finer work.

market.name: Market
market.description: Trades one resource for another, at better rates every level, and buys the hero's spare gear.
